subject: Contender pilot underway + staged-rollback term for renewal
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@novoretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — running a short pilot with Contender

Hey Soojin,

Quick update from our side: procurement gave the green light to run a short 2-week pilot with Contender (their price/throughput looked attractive on paper). We want to be transparent — this is exploratory, but there is real appetite to shift if the win is clear.

I attached the summary Contender shared so you can see the scope (they've suggested a synthetic workload + 24/7 traffic ramp). Can Redwood run a parallel validation with our actual production traces and produce a side-by-side on latency/cost per 1M tokens?

Also, procurement asked whether Redwood would consider a "staged rollback" clause: if Contender meets X threshold during the pilot and we still decide to move, we would require a 30-day rollback window with capacity guarantees and a mechanism for us to return traffic without immediate termination penalties.

Would appreciate a quick yes/no on doing the validation and a note on whether you can support a staged rollback construct.

Thanks,
Carlos
Head of Platform Engineering
NovoRetail

Attachment: contender-pilot-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@novoretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — running a short pilot with Contender

Carlos — thanks for flagging and for the heads-up. Sorry to hear you were pushed to run a competitive pilot, but appreciate the transparency. We can absolutely run an apples-to-apples validation against your production traces.

Immediate ask from our side: can you share the recent 7-day trace and an example prompt/workload mix (token lengths, peak qps windows)? I attached a small CSV with the fields we need to map to our test harness. If you can also confirm whether the Contender pilot is running on synthetic traffic vs replay, that will help tune the test.

On the staged rollback idea — we support a pragmatic, low-friction approach: 30-day pilot with a defined performance gate and a rollback window where you can shift traffic back to Redwood without financial penalty provided you meet the agreed thresholds. We usually put that in a short-term addendum (SLA credits + onboarding labor commitment). I'll loop Karthik and Marissa to draft language and pricing.

Next steps:
- Carlos: send traces + confirm pilot traffic type (replay vs synthetic)
- Karthik: can you scope an internal validation run (data movement, ephemeral infra) and rough ETA?
- Marissa: I'll need a preliminary counteroffer to present to procurement.

Available for a quick 30-min call this afternoon if that helps.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — running a short pilot with Contender

Looping in ops and pricing. Quick read: we can run a replay validation using a one-week trace and produce a side-by-side on latency percentiles, per-token cost, and cache hit rates. Rough resource estimate: 2x A40 equiv for 48 hours for the stress run, then a steady-state 24-hour run for cost numbers.

Suggested commercial approach (for Marissa):
- Offer a 12-month renewal with a 2x committed capacity uplift (to lock in throughput).
- Include a 30-day staged rollback addendum: customer may reduce traffic back to Redwood within 30 days of migration without early termination penalties if performance gates are invoked; Redwood will provide an onboarding window and SLA credits for missed targets.
- To sweeten: 10-15% rebate on committed spend if rollback occurs within the window; equivalent warm-standby cost if they need us to maintain capacity during the rollback window.

I'll prepare the test harness plan and estimate infra spend. If we want to be aggressive, we can offer an implementation credit that covers half the onboarding labor.

Karthik
Director, Platform Solutions

From: Beth Clarkson <beth@contender.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@novoretail.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contender pilot — test materials attached

Carlos — thanks for the intro. We pushed the pilot fixture to your environment early this morning. Attached a more detailed runbook and our baseline numbers. Happy to run the demo for your infra team tomorrow at 10am PT.

Soojin — we want this to be fair; we'll share raw logs and the synthetic workload config after the demo. If Redwood wants to run a replay, we'd welcome the side-by-side results.

Best,
Beth Clarkson
Head of Solutions, Contender AI
Beth@contender.ai

Attachment: contender-runbook-v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@novoretail.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-15T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood counterproposal for NovoRetail renewal (draft)

Carlos — appreciate you looping us in. Attached is a formal counterproposal for your renewal that incorporates the staged rollback language we discussed. High level:
- Term: 12 months (renewal effective 2028-05-01)
- Commit: 2x current baseline capacity (to guarantee headroom during migration)
- Price: $0.95 / 1k tokens for generation traffic, $0.35 / 1k tokens for embeddings (volume tiers included)
- Staged rollback addendum: 30-day window after migration where NovoRetail may return traffic to Redwood without termination penalty provided thresholds are met; Redwood will provide onboarding support and an SLA credit schedule if we miss targets.
- Implementation credit: $25K towards onboarding (to offset cutover cost)

We can also include a short proof-of-performance clause: Redwood will run a side-by-side replay validation and produce a results packet within 5 business days of receiving traces. If you prefer to formalize the rollback mechanics, I've attached a draft term sheet (staged-rollback-term-draft_v1.docx) and a PDF counterproposal for procurement.

If this looks directionally correct, let's schedule a procurement/counterparty call — I'm available Tuesday/Wednesday next week.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0142

Attachments: novoretail-renewal-counterproposal-2028-04-15.pdf (pdf), staged-rollback-term-draft_v1.docx (docx)

From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@novoretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, procurement@novoretail.com
Date: 2028-04-18T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood counterproposal for NovoRetail renewal (draft)

Marissa — thanks, that draft looks reasonable and thoughtful. I've pushed the PDF to procurement for review and asked them to validate the rollback mechanics. Procurement set a doc review for Thursday 4/20; they asked for the replay results packet before the call if possible.

We're scheduling the demo with Contender for tomorrow, and I'll share any initial impressions. For now, please go ahead with the replay validation once we send the traces (I'll ask infra to drop them in the shared drive).

Carlos
Head of Platform Engineering, NovoRetail
